<Route path="/ade/studio" />

Classes, properties, paths and operations are edited in **Studio**, the editing surface of the
**Designer** app. Designer is a separate, beta application, so it isn't part of the Control Panel.
An administrator gives each person access to it with
[Suite Access](../admin/users.mdx#give-a-user-suite-access). With Suite Access, **Designer** and
**Developer** appear in the **Build** section of the sidebar, and the launcher shows a
**Designer Suite** card. The **Designer** menu lists **Suite Home**, **Workspace**,
**Workspace · Paths** and **Code & exports**. Without Suite Access, none of these appears; ask an
administrator.

| Menu entry | Opens | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Suite Home** | Designer's home page | Suite Access |
| **Workspace** | Schemas and paths in one workspace | The Designer plan |
| **Workspace · Paths** | The same workspace, on its **Paths** lens | The Paths plan |
| **Code & exports** | The generated code and exports for a version | The Designer or the Paths plan |

An entry your plan does not include stays in the menu with a note on how to get it, but does not
open.

Links into Studio from the Control Panel use these routes, which open the same place in Designer:

| Route | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `/ade/studio/workspace` | The workspace |
| `/ade/studio/code` | The code view |
| `/ade/studio`, `/ade/studio/editor` | The workspace. Designer's separate class editor was removed; these older links still open |
| `/ade/studio/paths` | The workspace on its **Paths** lens. Designer's separate paths editor was removed; this older link still opens |

A link that names a project and version opens the workspace on them.

**Catalog items open read-only.** An item in the [Catalog](../bring-in/catalog.mdx) is not a
project yet, so its **“Open in Designer”** button opens Designer's `/catalog/{id}` page: the item's
normalized model and raw source, with no edit, save or publish. Convert it in the Catalog to edit it
— see [View an item in Designer](../bring-in/catalog.mdx#view-an-item-in-designer).

Designer's address comes from `NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDIO_URL` (default `https://suite.apiome.dev`).
Because Designer is not part of this installation, this site has no screenshots of it.

## The Suite link

A user licensed for the suite also gets a **Suite** link right under **Home** in the sidebar. It
opens the suite's home at the same address (`NEXT_PUBLIC_STUDIO_URL`, default
`https://suite.apiome.dev`) in a new tab.

The link appears only when the user's licence flags include `designer` or `paths` once
[Suite Access](../admin/users.mdx#give-a-user-suite-access) is applied. That is the same check that
shows **Designer** in **Build**. Without it, no link is drawn.

:::info Commercial application
The Apiome Suite is a commercial application. It is **not** part of the open-source Apiome project,
and none of its code ships in this repository. The open-source Control Panel only links to it, and
only when the right licensing flags are present.
:::

To edit without Designer, use the REST API or an import — the guides below show both.

- [Edit classes and properties](./edit-classes-and-properties.md)
- [Edit paths and operations](./edit-paths.md)

## With the API

`GET` / `POST /v1/classes/{tenant}`, `PUT /v1/classes/{tenant}/{class}`; `GET` / `POST
/v1/paths/{tenant}/{version}`, `PUT /v1/paths/{tenant}/{version}/{path}` — see the [API
reference](../reference/api-reference.md).
